title: Cardy's formula for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation
main_claim: For every bounded Jordan domain with four counterclockwise marks a,b,c,d, the annealed probability that the closed black-cell union in critical planar Poisson–Voronoi percolation crosses from arc ab to arc cd converges to Cardy's function F(x) of the marked conformal parameter. As a corollary, quenched crossing probabilities of fixed rectangles converge in L^2.

issues.description: The whole argument rests on three cited inputs that I could not check offline against the source: the alternating four-arm bound alpha_4 <= C(r/R)^{1+c_4} for Voronoi percolation, the quenched second-moment comparison E[p_j^2] <= C_j alpha_j^2 for every fixed j, and alpha_5 <= C(r/R)^2 for the paper's odd-j event (an extra black arm whose cells touch no other arm). The paper routes vertex-disjoint arms only through their own cells and shared open sides, which is consistent with that definition. Even so, the exact hypotheses of Vanneuville 2025 (Prop. 3.4(iii), Prop. 6.2, Prop. 3.14) are unverified here. The near-return and mixed-four-arm lemmas need these inputs.
issues.evidence: "The powers in (prob:arm-powers) are, respectively, [Vanneuville2025, (3.1), Proposition 3.4(iii), and Proposition 6.2]"

coverage:
I read all nine sections of the LaTeX source in build/sections. Here is what I checked in detail.
- Sec. 1: the two-defect bijection lemma. Finite orthogonality <Z_t,Z_u>=0 and ||Z_t||^2=3/4, including the star-port case analysis and the orientation reversal pi(j)=l-j that makes the three-through-path Fourier sum vanish. The decomposition into p_t and q_t, the identity |p|^2-|q|^2=(4/sqrt3)Area, the Bessel identities, the rim, no-bypass and sandwich lemmas, and the closed-sum tail proof (stationary measure intensity and eps-scaling).
- Sec. 2: the Reimer-to-product reduction, the colour-order (leftmost path) lemma, the strand reduction plus BK moment bound in the mixed-four-arms lemma, the A5-box-A1 construction in the near-return lemma, and the two-site gates.
- Sec. 3: cycle-experiment density domination, gate consistency, the state cochain (closed sum under bounded density, then resampling one sector plus Jensen to remove exterior dependence), common closure, and chart stability.
- Sec. 4: additivity, the rational-span linear extension and boundedness of a_h^X, the normalization a_h^V=1, the endpoint potentials defined as conditional expectations of the fixed insertions, the bias bound O(h(1+k)), and the spiral clearance computations.
- Sec. 5: the flag and preparation density bounds (preparation output pi(.|A) <= p_*^{-1} pi), the small-propensity discard inequality, and the block-chain density argument.
- Sec. 6: the dominated forcing kernel, the unnormalized-subprobability comparison giving I_X(gamma)=H_e^X pathwise, summation by parts (displacement and base potentials cancel), the error exponents r_h h^{-1+c}log^2 h and r_h h^{-1+c/2}, the mixed-atom dyadic Bessel refinement and its count C h^{-2+c}2^{-cj}, and the final a_h -> a step.
- Sec. 7: the algebra Re<V-2Q,V> = |U|^2-|Q|^2 = sqrt3 Area|f|^2, with the pairing limit giving 1-2Re a>0.
- Sec. 8: the closing-star observable as a mean partner label (degree-three probability 1/4), the side constraints and crossing coefficient, the identity U=(1-a)V-R used for the discrete Cauchy-Riemann relation, the edge-measure limit with df^dz=2i dbar f dA (sign checked), the boundary-uniqueness lemma, the Schwarz-Christoffel proportion, the Jordan buffer squeeze and the quenched-rectangle corollary.
Not independently verified: the cited Voronoi arm and crossing estimates, and the topological details of the twist classification and smoothing citations.
sibling_notes: The family 224 board held two companion papers, both reported no_gap_found: rank 39 (pivotal amplitude from Cardy's formula) and rank 58 (quenched near-critical universality). Both import results from this paper, so a gap here would spread to them. I found nothing that undermines those imports. The shared ingredients (orthogonal component fields, transport scalar a, arm inputs) look consistent across the three papers.
